title: Quantified level matrix and midpoint relation
statement: Let $w,r$ be natural numbers and let $E$ be a relation on pairs of finite Boolean strings. Define $\operatorname{Mid}_0(A,B)$ to mean $E(A,B)$; define $\operatorname{Mid}_{r+1}(A,B)$ to mean that some string $z$ of length $w$ satisfies both $\operatorname{Mid}_r(A,z)$ and $\operatorname{Mid}_r(z,B)$. For every position $p$, Boolean assignment $\sigma$, and strings $A,B$ of length $w$, the quantified formula with prefix consisting of $r$ repetitions of $w$ existential, $w$ universal, and $w$ universal quantifiers, and with matrix given by the recursively defined level matrix starting at position $p$ with endpoints $A,B$, is true under assignment $\sigma$ and starting index $p$ if and only if $\operatorname{Mid}_r(A,B)$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: A relation $E$ on pairs of finite Boolean strings
caveat: The recursive level matrix and selector definitions are provided formally but not informally in the payload; the sentence identifies their recursive role without expanding their block-selection formula.
